svg.aria-label: One hundred paper slips, one for each semicolon and colon pulled at random from 1700s English prose and coded twice, by two separate Claude agents that agreed on 95 of 100. Each turns over to pink if the mark glues two clauses that could each stand as a sentence, or dark if it separates a list, introduces a quotation, or sits in a heading or footnote. 43 of 60 semicolons glue two clauses (72%), and 23 of 40 colons do (58%).
